spans.text: How long does a sneeze last on paper?
The Library of Congress identifies forty-five frames of Fred Ott sneezing in a single photographic record.
In the Library’s moving-image catalog, the account of the viewing copy describes photographing the still image again.
That explains how a sequence on a page can become movement on a screen.
Let’s give our drawing two clocks.
Show every one of forty-five numbered cards for a fifteenth of a second, and the set lasts three seconds.
At thirty cards a second, exactly the same set lasts one and a half.
Which clock should we set for Ott?
These two catalog passages give us the pictures and a way to see them move.
They leave the speed of our reconstruction open.
